# loadFontFromUrl

<!-- Generated from the doc comments in the library. Do not edit this file. -->

Asynchronously fetches a TrueType font from a URL (browser) or file path (Node), parses it, and registers it so subsequent synchronous layout + rendering passes can use it without further async work.

Two registrations happen: 1. `FontMetrics.registerFontInstance(url, font)` - so any element whose `fontName` matches `url` (typical path-style identifier such as `/fonts/NotoEmoji-Regular.ttf`) gets accurate per-glyph width measurement, including supplementary-plane code points like emoji. 2. `FontManager.registerFont(bytes, { family, subfamily })` - so the same font is available for PDF/A standard-font substitution and for any element that references it by family name.

Call once at startup (or before each document generation) for every TTF the document will reference by URL/path. Then call `doc.generateAsync()` as normal - the layout engine itself stays synchronous.

Import from `@bonniepdf/core`.

```typescript
loadFontFromUrl(url: string, opts?: { family?: string; subfamily?: string; }): Promise<void>
```
